Speaker: AK
Manx: Va daa ben aegey, as v’ad sooree, soie sooree, as nane jeh’n deiney aegey,
English: There were two young women, and they were courting, sitting courting and one of the young men,

Speaker: AK
Manx: as v’eh geddyn g’accrys, as ren eh goll dy jeeaghyn dy geddyn bit dy vee,
English: was getting hungry, and he did go to look to get a bit of food,

Speaker: AK
Manx: as ooilley v’eh abyl dy geddyn as pot dy poddash pishyragh.
English: and all he was able to get, and a pot of peas porridge.

Speaker: AK
Manx: As v’eh gee eh gollrish jyst yn ’amman,
English: and he was eating it like a dish...

Speaker: AK
Manx: As v’eh goaill then, jyst lane da’n fer elley, as ren eh jarrood yn raad,
English: and he was then taking a bowl full to the other fellow, and he did forget the way, (in the house)

Speaker: AK
Manx: as ren eh goll da’n raad va’n Mainshter as yn Ben-ainshter cadley,
English: and he did go to where the Master and Mistress were sleeping,

Speaker: AK
Manx: ‘Shoh boy, gow shoh’, v’eh gra, as cha row veg cheet, ‘Shoh, gow shoh’,
English: ‘Here boy, take this’, he was saying, and there was nothing coming, ‘This, take this’,

Speaker: AK
Manx: as ren eh troggey yn curlead, curlead, as threw yn poddash pishyragh er y Ven-ainshter.
English: and he did lift the quilt, quilt, cover and threw the peas porridge on the Mistress.

Speaker: AK
Manx: ‘Juan’, t’ee gra, ‘T’eh moghree, t’eh traa geddyn seose, irree boy, irree boy’.
English: ‘John’, she was saying ‘It is morning, it’s time to get up, rise boy, rise boy’.

Speaker: AK
Manx: Well ren Juan geddyn irree ‘Aw! Chiarn. Aw, My Yee, Peggy’, ren eh gra ‘T’ou er keck ‘sy lhiabbee’!
English: Well John did get up, ‘Aw! Lord. Aw, my God, Peggy’, he did say, ‘You have shit in the bed’!

Speaker: AK
Manx: ‘Aw Chiarn, ta, she said, ‘Cha jeanym dy bragh, ny dy bragh ee poddash pishyragh reesht,
English: ‘Aw, Lord’, yes,’ she said, ‘I will not ever, not never eat peas porridge again,

Speaker: AK
Manx: son t’eh goll trooid mee gollrish myr v’eh geay’.
English: for it has gone through me like as it was wind’.

Speaker: MB
Manx: Aw, va shen mie
English: Aw, that was good.

Speaker: AK
Manx: Aw, son Laa Patrick ayns yn moghree va’n guoiee cheet
English: Aw, for Patrick’s Day, in the morning the geese were coming

Speaker: AK
Manx: woish Nerin, Nerin, as v’ad gra, ‘Cur huc eh, cur huc eh’,
English: from Ireland, Ireland, and they were saying ‘Give it to them, give it to them’

Speaker: AK
Manx: as v’ad goll thie ayns yn October, ‘Gow giare eh, gow giare eh’.
English: and they were going home in the October ‘Take it short, take it short’. (cut it short)

Speaker: AK
Manx: They were saying that. V’ad gra shen. They were cut off, cut off.
English: They were saying that.

Speaker: AK
Manx: Aw, shenn Nanny Sammy, as ren ee goll dys yn margey as ren ee creck yn booa,
English: Aw, old Nanny Sammy, and she did go to the market (fair) and she did sell the cow,

Speaker: AK
Manx: as traa ennagh elley ren ee, v’ee briaght jeh’n dooinney, v’ee briaght jeh’n dooinney,
English: and some other time she did enquire of the man, she was asking of the man,

Speaker: AK
Manx: ‘Cre’n aght ta’n booa, Juan?’
English: ‘What way (how) is the cow, Juan?’

Speaker: AK
Manx: ‘Aw, dy chooilley oayll aynjee’.
English: ‘Aw, every spell in her’.

Speaker: AK
Manx: ‘As c’red ta shiu? C’red’?
English: ‘And what are you? What’?
